titulo: Wikimedia Foundation closes Wikinews after 21 years

fuente.nota: Text shortened by removing paragraphs; the sentences are unchanged.

parrafos: The Board of Trustees of the Wikimedia Foundation announced on March 30 its decision to close all language editions of the project. In the announcement, a representative from Wikimedia Foundation cited motivations such as "long-term sustainability, levels of community activity, and the availability of reliable news coverage on other platforms". The announcement stated that all Wikinews editions—referring to the multiple language sections of Wikinews—would "transition to read-only mode" on May 4. The announcement did not mention the time zone when the wiki would go in read-only mode; but Wikinews operated under the UTC timezone.

In the announcement message, WMF trustee Victoria Doronina said, "We thank all contributors who have participated in Wikinews over the years and helped build a unique experiment in collaborative journalism within the Wikimedia movement. We understand that some of them may be disappointed by this decision. To our regret, the project wasn't able to fulfil its promise, and many of its functions were eclipsed by the notable news coverage in Wikipedias."

According to the WMF, most traffic to Wikinews came in the form of web crawlers and bots, as opposed to humans. Per the Wikimedia Cloud statistics in the past one year, both, English and Chinese Wikinews received more traffic from humans as compared to crawlers. The foundation stated in its closure recommendation that it is "difficult to claim that it is disseminating educational content and, even more so, that it is doing so effectively and globally."

On March 31, users from different countries and regions started discussions regarding moving the Wikinews content and community to another website at Wikimedia's Meta-Wiki. Miraheze and Wikimedia NYC were in discussion of continuing the hosting as Wikinews Pulse, with a restructure to increase multilingual support and try new outputs, according to a note by a Wikimedia volunteer User:Pharos. However, at the time of publishing this report, they had not provided an estimated time the project would be restarted.

Wikinews was a sister project of other Wikimedia initiatives. Some of the other sister projects includes Wikipedia, Wiktionary, and Wikimedia Commons. All of these Wikimedia projects support the dissemination of free knowledge and media. The future of Wikinews was raised for consideration in June, with a WMF task force recommending the project's closure, followed by a period of public consultation about Wikinews. After this process, the Board announced in March that the 31 active editions of Wikinews would be placed in read-only mode indefinitely.

Wikinews was launched in November 2004. It was first proposed by an anonymous contributor in January 2003 and faced a community vote that ended 151 yea and 59 nay, leading to the first demo going live in October 2004. The English-language Wikinews was formally created December 2 of that year, with German following one day later.

The project's early development followed a series of community discussions and milestones in late 2004 and early 2005. A non-binding straw poll on content licensing began on October 26, 2004, alongside discussions on the project's scope and policies. The initial demo site, hosted at demo.wikinews.org, was later moved to the English Wikinews domain on December 2 of that year.

Following the launch of the English and German editions in December 2004, additional language editions were created in early 2005, including Dutch, French, Swedish, Spanish, Bulgarian, Polish, Romanian, and Portuguese. The project also adopted a logo in February 2005 through a community voting process.

While many Wikinews articles were synthesized from other news sources, the project also posted original reporting. The purpose of this activity was to add exclusive content which would not be available elsewhere on the web or on television. These original reports included interviews with people such as Shimon Peres, then-president of Israel; U.S. Senator Sam Brownback; journalist Gay Talese; and voice actor Billy West. A 2005 article featuring original reporting, Unrest in Belize, was cited by Wikipedia co-founder Jimmy Wales as Wikinews's first scoop.

In 2008, Wikinews introduced a volunteer peer review process, with users voting to elect peer reviewers. From that time, a volunteer reviewer would have to approve each news report before it would be published; which would add 'Published' category to the article and display the article on the main page and RSS feeds. For some time, among others, the late Brian McNeil and then the late Pi zero led the project until 2021.

In a 2010 interview, researcher Andrew Lih from University of Hong Kong Journalism and Media Studies Centre, commented, "[I]t's not clear that the wiki process really gears itself towards deadlines and group narrative writing.... And I think that is providing some kind of a tension in terms of getting Wikipedians to write for an organization such as Wikinews." In 2013, a link to Wikinews was removed from the "In the News" section of the front page of Wikipedia, and links to Wikinews were also removed from the Current Events portal in that year.
titulo_es: The Wikimedia Foundation closes Wikinews after 21 years
resumen_es: The Wikimedia Foundation announces the closure of all editions of Wikinews, which will become read-only, because of their low activity and the news coverage available on other platforms. The article also reviews the history of the project since 2004 and its difficulties.

ideas_clave.idea: On 30 March the Wikimedia Foundation's board decided to shut down every language edition of Wikinews, which would become read-only on 4 May, citing sustainability, low participation and the availability of reliable news elsewhere.

A trustee thanked contributors while admitting that the project never fulfilled its potential, and the Foundation argued that most of its traffic came from automated programs rather than human readers.
Volunteers have started discussing how to move the content and community to another platform, possibly under the name Wikinews Pulse, though no relaunch date has been given.
As one of Wikipedia's sister projects, Wikinews was reviewed by a task force that recommended its closure, and after a public consultation its 31 active editions were frozen indefinitely.
The project, first suggested in 2003 and approved by a community vote, was launched in English and German at the end of 2004 and spread to many other languages in 2005.
Besides summarising other sources, Wikinews produced original reports and interviews, and from 2008 every article had to pass a volunteer peer review before publication.
Experts noted early on that the wiki model was ill-suited to news deadlines, and in 2013 Wikipedia removed links to Wikinews from its main news sections.

resumen_modelo: The article reports that the Wikimedia Foundation has decided to close all language editions of Wikinews, which were to switch to read-only mode on 4 May. The Foundation justified the decision by pointing to doubts about the project's sustainability, low community activity and the abundance of reliable news on other platforms, adding that most visits came from bots rather than people. Although one trustee thanked the volunteers, she admitted that the project had not lived up to its promise. Meanwhile, some volunteers are exploring ways of moving the content to a new site. The text then recalls the project's history: proposed in 2003 and approved by a community vote, Wikinews was launched in English and German in 2004 and soon expanded to other languages. In addition to summarising news from other sources, it published original reports and interviews and, from 2008, required each article to be approved by a volunteer reviewer. However, critics had long argued that the collaborative wiki model was poorly suited to the deadlines of journalism, and in 2013 Wikipedia stopped linking to it from its news sections.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: All Wikinews editions were to become read-only on 30 March.
preguntas.cita: would “transition to read-only mode” on May 4
preguntas.explicacion: 30 March is the date of the announcement; the switch to read-only mode was planned for 4 May.

preguntas.pregunta: Which reasons did the Foundation give for closing Wikinews?
opciones: Sustainability, community activity and reliable news available elsewhere
Lack of funding and legal disputes
respuestas: Sustainability, community activity and reliable news available elsewhere
preguntas.cita: long-term sustainability, levels of community activity, and the availability of reliable news coverage on other platforms
preguntas.explicacion: These are the three reasons given in the announcement. Funding, lawsuits, copyright and outside pressure are not mentioned.

preguntas.enunciado: Find a word in paragraph 1 that means “overshadowed, surpassed by something else”.
preguntas.pregunta: Find a word meaning 'overshadowed, made less important'.
preguntas.cita: many of its functions were eclipsed by the notable news coverage in Wikipedias
preguntas.explicacion: “Eclipsed” is used figuratively: Wikipedia's coverage of current events pushed Wikinews into the background.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: According to the Foundation, most of Wikinews' traffic came from bots and web crawlers.
preguntas.cita: most traffic to Wikinews came in the form of web crawlers and bots, as opposed to humans
preguntas.explicacion: This is what the Foundation claims. The text then adds that the English and Chinese editions received more human traffic, which qualifies that argument.

preguntas.pregunta: Who was discussing the possibility of continuing the project as Wikinews Pulse?
opciones: The Wikimedia Foundation's Board of Trustees
The English and Chinese Wikinews communities
preguntas.cita: Miraheze and Wikimedia NYC were in discussion of continuing the hosting as Wikinews Pulse
preguntas.explicacion: It is Miraheze and Wikimedia NYC that are negotiating to host the project. The board is the body closing it, and Wikipedia and Wiktionary are sister projects.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: The Wikimedia Foundation has offered to fund Wikinews Pulse.
preguntas.explicacion: The text says nothing about the Foundation funding the new project; it only mentions talks between volunteers and other organisations.

preguntas.pregunta: How many active editions of Wikinews were placed in read-only mode?
preguntas.cita: the 31 active editions of Wikinews would be placed in read-only mode indefinitely
preguntas.explicacion: There were 31 active editions. 151 and 59 are the votes for and against in 2003-2004, and 21 is the number of years the project lasted.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: The English edition of Wikinews was created one day after the German edition.
preguntas.cita: The English-language Wikinews was formally created December 2 of that year, with German following one day later.
preguntas.explicacion: It is the other way round: the English edition was created on 2 December and the German one a day later.

preguntas.explicacion: A “straw poll” is an indicative vote with no binding effect, as the adjective “non-binding” confirms.

To compete with Wikipedia for readers
respuestas: To provide exclusive content not available elsewhere
preguntas.cita: The purpose of this activity was to add exclusive content which would not be available elsewhere on the web or on television.
preguntas.explicacion: The text states explicitly that the aim was to offer exclusive content. The other purposes are not mentioned.

preguntas.explicacion: In journalism, a “scoop” is an exclusive story.

preguntas.pregunta: What change did Wikinews introduce in 2008, and how did it affect publication?
respuestas: It introduced a volunteer peer review system: an elected reviewer had to approve each report before it was published and displayed on the main page and RSS feeds.
preguntas.cita: a volunteer reviewer would have to approve each news report before it would be published
preguntas.explicacion: The answer should mention voluntary peer review and its consequence: no article was published without prior approval.

preguntas.enunciado: Answer in your own words (1–3 sentences).
preguntas.pregunta: According to Andrew Lih, why was the wiki model problematic for a news project?
respuestas: Because the wiki process is not designed for tight deadlines or for writing a collective narrative, which made it hard to get Wikipedia contributors to write news for Wikinews.
preguntas.cita: not clear that the wiki process really gears itself towards deadlines and group narrative writing
preguntas.explicacion: Lih points to the tension between the slow, collaborative pace of the wiki and journalism's demand for immediacy.
